key_insight: Func-R1 improves multimodal mathematical function reasoning by explicitly separating visual perception from symbolic reasoning and training the model to attend to the right visual evidence.
engineering_relevance: The paper shows that carefully designed post-training can reduce modality interference in MLLMs, which is important for building reliable AI assistants for STEM tasks involving charts, formulas, and diagrams.
method: Uses an explicitly decoupled architecture to separate perception from reasoning.
Applies a hierarchical post-training pipeline to first identify critical visual evidence, then perform deeper theoretical reasoning.
Introduces Perception-Aligned Theoretic Optimization (PATO) to align policy updates with mathematical properties while correcting visual input errors during reasoning.
evidence_signal: The method was evaluated on diverse benchmarks and is reported to achieve the best performance among open-source MLLMs, including an 8.4% gain over GPT-5 on MathVerse function-oriented tasks.
watch_item: The approach likely depends on high-quality visual cue extraction, so performance may degrade when inputs are noisy, ambiguous, or visually complex.
paper_title: Func-R1: Incentivizing Mathematical Function Reasoning in Multimodal Large Language Models
